newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine weather outlook seen positive for grains.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine weather outlook seen positive for grains.

text.p: Warm weather in Ukraine's grain regions later this week should allow farmers to speed up the spring sowing campaign, Anatoliy Prokopenko, deputy head of the National Weather Forecasting Centre, said on Monday.

"In the next few days we are forecasting cooler, rainy conditions in most of the regions," he said. "The weather will get better in the second half of this week because there will be more sun and warmth. That will speed up the sowing campaign."
Prokopenko said that the completion of the sowing campaign for spring grains, excluding maize, was slightly delayed because fields were wet due to recent continuous rains.
But he said the rains were not endangering spring sowing.
He also said that a prolonged winter was good for the winter grain crop because it provided necessary moisture in the soil.
"Winter grain is doing well because of that," he said.
Sugar beet sowing had not yet started due to wet conditions, but should get started at the end of the month or at the beginning of May.
The rain was viewed as good for the grain harvest overall, despite causing some delays to the spring grain sowing campaign.
It suggested there would not be a repeat of last May's drought, which was blamed for a slump in 1996 grain output to 25.4 million tonnes from 36.5 million tonnes in 1995, industry sources said.
